create.name: Guo Gu
create.bio:
Guo Gu is a teacher of Chan, the Chinese school of Buddhism from which Japanese Zen grew, and a scholar of the tradition. Raised in Taiwan, he was given his first meditation instruction at the age of four by the ascetic master Guangqin. After his family moved to the United States in 1980 he trained under Chan Master Sheng Yen, took monastic vows in 1991 and became Sheng Yen's first personal attendant, later receiving his permission to teach. In 2000 he set aside his robes, earned a doctorate in Buddhist Studies at Princeton, and now holds a professorship at Florida State University.

His teaching rests on the two classic Chan methods, silent illumination and huatou or koan practice, taught in plain, practical terms with attention to the body. He founded the Tallahassee Chan Center in Florida, where he gives talks and answers questions in person and over Zoom, and he has guided the London Chan Meditation group since 2014. He leads silent retreats of several days at centres across North America and in Britain. He also started Dharma Relief, which joins Buddhist groups of different lineages in service. His books with Shambhala are Passing Through the Gateless Barrier, Silent Illumination and The Essence of Chan, and he has also translated and edited several of Sheng Yen's works.

books.title: Passing Through the Gateless Barrier: Koan Practice for Real Life
books.author: Guo Gu
books.description: His own English version of the 48 cases in the thirteenth-century Gateless Barrier, each followed by commentary on working with it in meditation. It treats the old stories as live material for practice today rather than as historical puzzles.

books.title: Silent Illumination: A Chan Buddhist Path to Natural Awakening
books.author: Guo Gu
books.description: Instruction in the Chan method of silent illumination, built around translated passages from the twelfth-century master Hongzhi Zhengjue with Guo Gu's comments on each. A short, practical guide for people who want to try the method themselves.

books.title: The Essence of Chan: A Guide to Life and Practice according to the Teachings of Bodhidharma
books.author: Guo Gu
books.description: A compact introduction to Chan built on a short text attributed to Bodhidharma, the figure honoured as the first Chan ancestor. It explains the outlook and the practices together, with an eye to ordinary daily life.

courses.title: Gateway to Chan Hybrid Retreat (Barre Center for Buddhist Studies)
courses.description: A six-day retreat led by Guo Gu in Barre, Massachusetts, which can also be joined on Zoom. Days are mostly silent, with half-hour sitting periods broken up by gentle yoga and walking, and talks in the evenings. Meant for people who have already done at least one residential retreat of six days.
courses.price: $189 to $299 USD online; $695 to $1,495 USD residential; $425 USD commuter (sliding scale)

courses.title: Silent Illumination
courses.description: A recorded video course of twelve hours, filmed over six weeks in 2021, on the Chan method of silent illumination. It moves from relaxing and settling the body into more direct ways of contemplating experience. Self-paced, through the Tallahassee Chan Center.

courses.title: The Gateless Barrier: Forty-Eight Lectures on Kōans
courses.description: Recorded lectures working through each of the forty-eight cases in the Gateless Barrier, the classic koan collection that Guo Gu has also translated in book form. A course for those who want to study koan practice in depth at their own pace.

courses.title: Three Gates of Chan
courses.description: A one-hour recorded video course introducing the three main meditation methods used in Chan: following the breath, silent illumination and huatou. A good first step for newcomers to his teaching.

courses.title: The Platform Scripture of the Sixth Patriarch of Chan
courses.description: Nine hours of recorded audio on the Platform Scripture, the text that tells the life and teaching of Huineng and helped shape Chan as a school. Guo Gu draws out the points that matter most for practice.

courses.title: Mind, Mental Factors, and Emotions
courses.description: A fourteen-hour recorded audio course on the Yogācāra, or Consciousness-Only, map of the mind and its states. It looks at how emotions arise and how to meet them in daily life and practice.

free_resources.title: Guo Gu on Insight Timer
free_resources.description: A small set of his guided Chan meditations and short talks, among them a foundational sitting practice and a loving-kindness meditation. Free to play in the app or a browser.

free_resources.title: Guo Gu's Dharma Talks and Videos
free_resources.description: A page on his own site that gathers free recordings: guided sittings, talk series on the Heart Sutra and on koans, question-and-answer sessions and conversations with other Zen teachers. New videos are featured each month.

free_resources.title: The Way of Chan with Guo Gu (podcast)
free_resources.description: A free podcast carrying his recent talks, lectures and question-and-answer sessions. It is also on Spotify, Amazon and iHeartRadio.

free_resources.title: One Minute Chan
free_resources.description: A short daily practice he suggests on his site: pick five moments in the day and spend a minute in each simply relaxing and being with what you are doing. The same page explains what Chan is and lists his upcoming talks and retreats.
